human.problem: This two-blank card ('all the surrounding nations are ___ and ___') sets 'afraid' as blank 1 and 'disheartened' as blank 2. Either order makes sense, so a baker who picks 'disheartened' then 'afraid' could fairly argue they got it right but would be marked wrong. The no-near-matches rule only covers wrong answers. No rule covers two right answers that can swap places.
human.question: When the two blanks of a fill-in-the-blank card can swap places, should the card be rewritten so the order is clear, or should either order count as right?
